location.anchor_text: they emerge from the same side, subtending an angle of about 120 degrees rather than 180

findings.observation: The most spatial section in the chapter has the longest prose (5360 characters at the expanded tier) and exactly one figure: an unannotated crystal-structure still hotlinked from cdn.rcsb.org. Four inherently geometric claims are made with no visual support — that the strands are antiparallel, that the two glycosidic bonds of a pair subtend about 120 degrees and therefore produce one wide and one narrow groove, that base pairs stack 3.4 angstroms apart roughly perpendicular to the axis, and that the major groove presents four distinguishable donor/acceptor/methyl patterns while the minor groove does not.
findings.learner_impact: The 120-degree argument is the only derivation in the chapter that explains why grooves exist at all, and it is the sort of claim a reader either sees in one glance or never believes. On the supplied still, the major and minor grooves are present but unlabelled and, at that rendering size, not obviously unequal; the antiparallel direction is not marked at either end; and the major-groove readout pattern is not visible at all. The section that most needs a picture has the thinnest visual layer in the chapter.
findings.evidence: Section nugget-dna-double-helix-and-base-stacking contains exactly three blocks: blk-5o9wf2fc (text), blk-gs5dxm9v (image, url https://cdn.rcsb.org/images/structures/1bna_assembly-1.jpeg, no attribution field), blk-0rfpxvzk (external link). The asset's own long_description concedes "The image is a still rendering and conveys no motion or colour-coded sequence information." The section-1 schematic helix asset clip-dna-double-helix likewise concedes it "does not depict... the two grooves of differing width", and it is not used in this section.
findings.recommended_outcome: A reader needs to see, at minimum, the strand-direction labels at both ends of a duplex and the geometric origin of groove asymmetry — the two glycosidic bonds leaving a pair on the same side. The stacking distance and the major-groove information argument are secondary. Note also that this single figure is the chapter's only externally hosted image, so it is the one figure that can fail to load in the installable reader.

location.anchor_text: The alkoxide attacks phosphorus **in line** with the 5'-oxygen of the following residue

findings.observation: Both mechanisms taught in the chapter turn on a spatial relationship that no figure depicts. For RNA cleavage: the 2'-alkoxide sits two atoms from its target, held rigid by the furanose, and attacks in line with the departing 5'-oxygen through a five-membered ring closure. For chain extension: the 3'-hydroxyl attacks the alpha phosphorus in line with the leaving pyrophosphate through a trigonal-bipyramidal arrangement with inversion at phosphorus. The only structural figures supplied are the isolated starting material (uridine) and the isolated product (uridine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate); the geometry between them is prose-only. The chapter itself concedes the point: "it is worth drawing for yourself rather than reading."
findings.learner_impact: "In line" and "two atoms apart" and "trigonal bipyramidal" are claims about arrangement in space; a reader who cannot construct that arrangement from a sentence has nothing to fall back on, and the chapter's strongest explanatory move — that the reaction is fast because the nucleophile is tethered in the right orientation, not because it is a better nucleophile — becomes an assertion. Telling a reader to draw it themselves presumes the very skill the figure would build.
findings.evidence: Section nugget-rna-versus-dna-hydrolytic-stability figures: clip-rna-single-strand, mol-uridine, mol-uridine-23-cyclic-phosphate, mol-adenosine, mol-2-deoxyadenosine, mol-dinucleotide-dapdt — all single static structures, none showing the alkoxide, the attack trajectory, or the DNA control case side by side. Section nugget-chain-extension-at-phosphorus figures: mol-atp, mol-dinucleotide-dapdt, mol-damp — none shows the 3'-OH and the alpha phosphorus in the same drawing. No curved-arrow or transition-state asset exists in the package.
findings.recommended_outcome: The two substitutions at phosphorus need the nucleophile, the electrophilic phosphorus, and the leaving group visible in one frame with their relative arrangement apparent; the DNA control (hydrogen where the nucleophile would be) is the natural companion. The chapter's decision to omit a reaction-coordinate diagram is right and should be kept — no energy profile is taught — but the omission of any arrow-pushing or geometry figure is a genuine gap here rather than an appropriate restraint.

location.anchor_text: Select every statement below that reads that pattern correctly off the structures.

findings.observation: Two questions instruct the student to work from structures that the question does not show. ch28-pairing-donors-acceptors says "reads that pattern correctly off the structures" and ch28-mismatch-failure-mode says "Working from the structures rather than from memory", yet each item's own accessible_description states "no structures are shown". Across the whole 46-question set only four items carry any structure at all (two hotspot, two error_repair), plus two blank-canvas structure_scaffold items.
findings.learner_impact: The stem promises a reading task and delivers a recall task, which both misleads the student about how the item will be graded and quietly abandons the chapter's central pedagogical claim that the pairing rules are derivable. It also makes the assessment surface a poor rehearsal of the skill the reader prose is trying to build.
findings.evidence: compiled/question-set.json — ch28-pairing-donors-acceptors (multi_select, student_config keys: options only, accessible_description: "...no structures are shown"); ch28-mismatch-failure-mode (single_select, same). By contrast ch28-rna-cleavage-intermediate attaches structure_smiles to all four options and ch28-alpha-phosphorus-hotspot supplies molecule_smiles, so per-item structures are clearly supported by the platform.
findings.recommended_outcome: Items whose stems tell the student to read a structure must present the structure to read; otherwise the stems should stop claiming they do. The two questions in question are the ones that most directly rehearse the donor/acceptor skill, so they are the highest-value place to close the gap.

location.anchor_text: Find the single change from thymidine and see why a chain that has incorporated this residue cannot be extended.

findings.observation: The analogue section asks for comparisons against reference structures it does not supply, and supplies a reference structure nobody asked for. Zidovudine's caption says "Find the single change from thymidine" but thymidine appears only in section 3, six sections earlier. Acyclovir's and dideoxyadenosine's captions likewise invite comparison. The reference structure that is provided, 2'-deoxyadenosine, is placed last — after all three analogues — and is the wrong comparator for two of them (AZT is a thymidine analogue, acyclovir a guanosine analogue).
findings.learner_impact: A one-change comparison only works if both structures are in view at once. As ordered, a reader must hold AZT in memory, scroll back six sections to thymidine, and return; most will simply accept the prose statement, which is precisely the memorise-don't-derive behaviour the section is arguing against.
findings.evidence: Section nugget-nucleoside-analogue-drugs block order: blk-m2dlphqz (mol-zidovudine), blk-82hw2jpe (mol-acyclovir), blk-ty9cuwzj (mol-dideoxyadenosine), blk-uorhywcp (mol-2-deoxyadenosine). mol-thymidine is bound only to nugget-n-glycosidic-bond; mol-guanine appears only in sections 2 and 5.
findings.recommended_outcome: Each analogue needs its actual natural counterpart adjacent to it at the moment of comparison, in the order reference-then-analogue. The trailing 2'-deoxyadenosine as currently placed is not doing that job for any of the three.

location.anchor_text: Compare with the lactam figure and see that moving one hydrogen exchanges a donor for an acceptor at every position along the pairing edge.

findings.observation: The chapter's one deliberate side-by-side comparison is not side by side. The lactim tautomer's caption instructs the reader to compare it with the lactam figure, but the two are separated by four intervening structures: the order is adenine, guanine-lactam, cytosine, thymine, uracil, guanine-lactim. The tautomer discussion is also the last two paragraphs of the section's text block, so the reader meets the lactam figure long before the prose that motivates it.
findings.learner_impact: A donor/acceptor reversal that hinges on the position of a single hydrogen is only visible in direct juxtaposition. Separated by four other heterocycles that all look broadly similar at a glance, the comparison collapses into two unrelated pictures, and the chapter's stated stake — "Draw the wrong tautomer and every base pair you construct from it will be wrong" — is left unillustrated.
findings.evidence: Section nugget-purine-and-pyrimidine-bases block order: blk-svvsfaxs (adenine), blk-ketx5kka (guanine lactam), blk-cyqo8f3t (cytosine), blk-ycisjqh6 (thymine), blk-jpalo1sm (uracil), blk-t6apxlnl (guanine lactim). Compare with the correctly adjacent pairs elsewhere: ribofuranose then 2-deoxyribofuranose in section 1, adenosine then 2'-deoxyadenosine in section 3.
findings.recommended_outcome: The lactam and lactim need to be adjacent and explicitly marked as a matched pair, with the position of the moved hydrogen and the resulting donor/acceptor swap identifiable. The rest of the section's figure order is fine.

location.anchor_text: See the phosphate ester at the 5' position that turns a nucleoside into a nucleotide, and note the free 3' hydroxyl left available for the backbone.

findings.observation: Thirty-three molecule blocks are drawn from twenty unique assets, and the repeats carry byte-identical captions rather than a re-purposed one. mol-damp appears four times (sections 1, 4, 8, 10), mol-2-deoxyadenosine three times (3, 7, 9), mol-dinucleotide-dapdt three times (4, 7, 8), mol-adenosine three times (1, 3, 7), and the four bases twice each (2, 5). Several repeats are off-topic where they land: dAMP in the Sanger/phosphoramidite section teaches nothing about dideoxy terminators, DMT protection or P(III) coupling, and 2'-deoxyadenosine in the analogue section is the wrong comparator (see vis-008).
findings.learner_impact: Repeating a structure with the same caption trains the reader to skip figures, because by the third appearance the block predictably contains nothing new. That habit then costs them at the figures that do carry new information. It also inflates the apparent visual density of sections whose real visual coverage is thin.
findings.evidence: Reader block ids per asset — mol-damp: blk-jz9lu5iw, blk-arerx4at, blk-gs00xkkc, blk-7bw114vr, all with description "See the phosphate ester at the 5' position that turns a nucleoside into a nucleotide..."; mol-dinucleotide-dapdt: blk-hyi4aoq4, blk-4vzx6u4g, blk-egs4lnmd, all with the same description string.
findings.recommended_outcome: A repeated structure should either earn its second appearance by asking the reader to see something new in it, or be dropped. Trimming here also frees attention for the sections identified in vis-003, vis-005 and vis-006, which are genuinely under-illustrated.

location.anchor_text: Every internucleotide linkage therefore carries one full negative charge

findings.observation: Every phosphorus-containing figure is drawn in the neutral, fully protonated form, while the surrounding prose insists on the anionic form as its central teaching point. The package's long_description for each of these assets explains the choice ("the neutral form is drawn here so that every bond to phosphorus is visible"), but the compiled reader molecule block carries only name, smiles, alt_text and description — long_description is not among the emitted fields — so that reconciliation never reaches the student.
findings.learner_impact: The backbone section's argument, and four of its downstream consequences (electrophoresis mobility, counterion requirement, salt-dependent melting, lysine/arginine-rich DNA-binding proteins), all rest on one negative charge per linkage. The reader is looking at P–OH while reading that the group is completely deprotonated at any physiological pH, with nothing on the page to reconcile the two. The same mismatch recurs for the triphosphate in the chain-extension section, where the prose calls it "essentially fully deprotonated".
findings.evidence: mol-dinucleotide-dapdt, mol-damp, mol-atp, mol-uridine-23-cyclic-phosphate SMILES all use P(=O)(O)O neutral forms; each asset's long_description contains the explanation, and none of that text appears in the compiled blocks (blk-hyi4aoq4, blk-arerx4at, blk-wx90p1gy, blk-o366pb0x each have content keys alt_text, description, generator_href, name, smiles only).
findings.recommended_outcome: The student needs the drawn protonation state reconciled with the prose at the point of use — either by drawing the ionised form where the charge is the lesson, or by making the drawing convention explicit in text the reader actually sees. Silently contradicting the section's headline claim is the one outcome to avoid.

location.anchor_text: Antiparallel strands, two grooves, and the role of stacking

findings.observation: Every section is compiled as one long text block followed by a stack of figures at the end, so no figure is ever adjacent to the sentence it supports. At the default expanded detail tier the text blocks run 3300 to 6842 characters; a reader working through the donor/acceptor derivation in section 5 must scroll past roughly 4400 characters before reaching the adenine structure that derivation is about.
findings.learner_impact: The reader has to hold a structural description in working memory across a long scroll and then reconstruct which paragraph each trailing figure belongs to — the reconstruction cost the figure was supposed to remove. It also means the detail-tier control has an odd effect: a reader on the terse tier (515-792 characters) gets the same full stack of figures with captions written for the expanded narrative.
findings.evidence: All ten sections have exactly one text block in first position followed by media; _detail_texts lengths per section (terse/standard/expanded) run 515/1614/3300 up to 792/2771/6842. Section nugget-dna-double-helix-and-base-stacking has 5360 expanded characters ahead of its single figure.
findings.recommended_outcome: Figures need to sit near the prose they serve, or the prose needs an explicit in-text pointer to the figure below it. This is a layout/compilation need rather than an authoring one, and it affects every section in the chapter.

location.anchor_text: Fix the overall shape in mind before taking a single residue apart

findings.observation: The chapter's opening figure is a stylised ribbon helix placed in the section that is about taking one residue apart into base, sugar and phosphate — three things the drawing does not show. Its own long_description concedes it "does not depict individual atoms, the two grooves of differing width, or which base occupies any particular rung", and its alt text asserts a right-handed spiral that a reader cannot verify from a stylised drawing. The same asset is absent from section 6, the section that actually teaches helix geometry.
findings.learner_impact: As an advance organiser the figure is defensible, but as placed it is the only figure a reader meets before four unlabelled structures, and it carries no information the section uses. Meanwhile the section that would benefit from a schematic-versus-crystal-structure contrast has only the crystal structure.
findings.evidence: clip-dna-double-helix is bound to concept nucleoside-and-nucleotide-anatomy only; rendered as blk-181nbgat in section 1. The section-1 prose covers base/sugar/phosphate identity, nucleoside-versus-nucleotide naming, ribose-versus-deoxyribose, prime numbering, and alpha/beta/gamma phosphates — none of which the drawing depicts.
findings.recommended_outcome: Either this figure earns its slot by carrying something section 1 actually teaches — the three-part decomposition of one residue, which no current figure shows — or it belongs alongside the crystal structure in section 6 where schematic and real geometry can be contrasted.

location.anchor_text: dATP, dGTP, dCTP, or dTTP for DNA

findings.observation: The incoming monomer for the chain-extension section is illustrated with adenosine 5'-triphosphate — the ribo compound, carrying a 2'-hydroxyl — in a chapter whose preceding section has just established that the 2'-hydroxyl is the single feature that makes a nucleic acid self-destruct, and whose worked mechanism is framed around DNA polymerases. The same ribo structure is the stimulus for the hotspot question ch28-alpha-phosphorus-hotspot.
findings.learner_impact: A reader who has been trained across two sections to look for the 2' position will find one on the structure labelled as the incoming monomer, in a section that names dATP/dGTP/dCTP/dTTP in its second paragraph. It is a small mismatch but it lands exactly on the feature the chapter has made most salient.
findings.evidence: mol-atp SMILES Nc1ncnc2c1ncn2[C@@H]1O[C@H](COP(=O)(O)OP(=O)(O)OP(=O)(O)O)[C@@H](O)[C@H]1O (2'-OH present); reader block blk-wx90p1gy in nugget-chain-extension-at-phosphorus; ch28-alpha-phosphorus-hotspot molecule_smiles is the same string.
findings.recommended_outcome: The figure carrying the alpha/beta/gamma lesson should not silently contradict the DNA framing of the section it sits in, or the text should say plainly that ATP is being used as the generic triphosphate and that the DNA case lacks the 2'-hydroxyl.

strengths: Every asset carries specific, structural alt text rather than a generic label — mol-adenine's names the fused bicycle, the exocyclic amino group and the N-H position, and the reader block preserves it.

Both tautomers of guanine are actually drawn. The chapter does not merely assert that the lactam dominates; it supplies the lactim so the donor/acceptor reversal is a visible comparison (placement aside, see vis-009).

Two one-atom comparisons are correctly built as adjacent pairs: ribofuranose then 2-deoxyribofuranose in section 1, and adenosine then 2'-deoxyadenosine in section 3. That is the right pattern and it works.
The RNA cleavage intermediate is given a structure of its own (mol-uridine-23-cyclic-phosphate), so the classical 2'/3' mixture evidence has something concrete attached to it.

ch28-rna-cleavage-intermediate attaches structure_smiles to all four options, and ch28-alpha-phosphorus-hotspot supplies molecule_smiles — the two items where structural discrimination is genuinely the task do show structures.

The decision to include no reaction-coordinate diagram is correct restraint, not a gap. The chapter's only energetic claims are that the polymerisation step is near thermoneutral and that pyrophosphate hydrolysis pulls it forward; an energy profile would add a spurious barrier picture the chapter never argues for.

Each deferred video brief records a production_note naming the reader section that carries the same content in prose, so the authoring intent was explicitly not to strand the material behind an animation.
open_questions: Does the reader support any block type capable of rendering a synthesis_roadmap spec, or is a pre-rendered static image the only route for roadmap-phosphoramidite-cycle? This decides whether vis-002 is a compiler fix or an asset-production fix.

Can authored per-figure rdkit_options or reactive-site highlight parameters reach reader molecule blocks? The compiler emitted none for any of the 20 molecule assets, and I could not determine whether the reader block schema plumbs anything beyond rdkit_options through to the render endpoint. This bears directly on vis-004.

Is the cdn.rcsb.org hotlink for pdb-b-dna-dodecamer intended to be cached for the installable reader, and does the image block need an attribution field? The two clipart image blocks carry attribution and this one does not — flagged as an observation, not a rights judgement.

The NIAID schematic's alt text asserts a right-handed spiral. I inspected the PNG and could not confidently confirm handedness from the stylised drawing; someone should verify rather than take the alt text's word for it.
vis-012 is filed under cognitive-load because no figure-placement category exists in the schema. If figure placement recurs across chapters it may deserve its own id.

executive_summary: Chemically this is the strongest chapter reviewed to date: the instructor persona independently re-parsed all 20 SMILES with RDKit and confirmed every InChIKey, every beta-anomeric assignment, the dinucleotide's 3'-to-5' connectivity and free-end identity, and both hotspot answer keys. All 46 answer keys pass referential integrity, no accessible_description leaks an answer, and no hint contains its own answer. One chemical blocker exists and is chapter-authored and bounded: two strand-directionality questions name DNA residues with ribonucleoside names ("the adenosine residue" in a strand containing thymine), and one distractor describes a 2'-oxygen that a DNA residue does not have — which contradicts the chapter's own practice check. The verdict is nonetheless blocked rather than major revision, because two required-access blockers are unresolved and are platform-level: the hotspot items expose atom targets whose only accessible name is an element-plus-index string with no disclosed mapping to the chemical position the prompt names, and the structure_scaffold items offer no answer channel except a pointer-driven drawing canvas. Both recur from chapters 1, 11, and 15 through 19. The dominant non-blocking theme is unanimous across all four personas: the chapter teaches two mechanisms and a hydrogen-bonded pair entirely in prose, and no figure anywhere shows two bases facing each other, either mechanism's electron flow, or the in-line geometry at phosphorus — while the one genuinely sequential figure that was authored, the phosphoramidite roadmap, reaches the reader as an empty image container.
consensus_strengths: Chemical accuracy is exceptional: 20/20 SMILES verified by independent RDKit re-parse, correct lactam tautomers throughout, correct donor/acceptor assignments on both pairing edges, correct N9/N1 attachment, and both hotspot atom indices correct.
Every one of the 23 surfaced questions carries a genuinely progressive three-level hint ladder and wrong-answer explanations that diagnose the specific error rather than restating the prompt.

The prose names each misconception before the student can make it, in bold and in advance ('Hydrogen bonding is not what holds the duplex together'; 'Students look for the reactive carbon and there is not one').
All 24 assets carry both alt_text and long_description that convey real chemistry and are explicitly honest about what the image does not show.

Nothing in the chapter depends on colour, motion, hover, or spatial position as a sole carrier of meaning; rank_order, categorize_groups, matching_pairs, comparison_matrix and error_repair are keyboard-complete by construction.
The decision to author no reaction-coordinate diagram is correct restraint rather than an omission — the chapter makes no energy-profile argument that one would serve.

ranked_recommendations.title: DNA residues are named as ribonucleosides in both strand-directionality questions
ranked_recommendations.need: Assessment must stop contradicting the chapter's own teaching that a ribonucleoside cannot appear in DNA; and a distractor must describe a structure that is wrong rather than impossible.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: The chemistry, the keys and the reasoning are all correct — only the residue names and one distractor's premise are wrong. Renaming to the 2'-deoxy compounds and re-anchoring the 2'-oxygen distractor fully resolves the contradiction without touching the item design, so no rewrite or replacement is warranted.

ranked_recommendations.title: Hotspot atom targets carry no chemical identity for a non-visual learner
ranked_recommendations.need: A learner who cannot see the structure needs a disclosed, stable correspondence between the chemical positions the prompt names and the selectable targets.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Platform-level: the renderer generates accessible names from the RDKit heavy-atom index. No chapter edit can supply the mapping, because the atom numbering is a traversal artefact rather than a chemical locant. Escalated as the same ticket already open from ch11/15/16.

ranked_recommendations.title: structure_scaffold has no non-pointer, non-visual answer channel
ranked_recommendations.need: The 'produce a structure' skill needs an answer route that does not require a pointing device or sight, or an equivalent item assessing the same decisions.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Platform-level and identical to the open ticket from ch1/11/15/16/17/18/19. Within the chapter the least-complex mitigation is that the same lactam/ring/substituent decisions are already assessed by ch28-lactam-tautomer and ch28-purine-pyrimidine-sort, so an instructor can build a complete assignment without the drawing items.

ranked_recommendations.title: No figure shows two bases hydrogen bonded to each other
ranked_recommendations.need: The chapter's headline skill is deriving A-T and G-C by reading donor/acceptor patterns off structures; that derivation is currently performable only in the head.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: All four personas independently reached this. A description cannot substitute, because the thing to be learned is a spatial registry between two edges — the one case in this chapter where prose provably cannot carry the idea. Needs A-T, G-C and at least one rejected pair, with donors and acceptors labelled in text rather than by colour.

ranked_recommendations.title: Neither mechanism is drawn anywhere
ranked_recommendations.need: Two concepts carry objectives that begin 'Draw the mechanism...' and 'Write the chain-extension step...', and the chapter models neither; only start and end states are shown.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: A stepwise static sequence satisfies both objectives and, unlike the deferred animations, is producible now and is accessible without motion. Full animation is not required — the objectives ask the student to draw, so what they need is a worked drawing to model.

ranked_recommendations.title: The phosphoramidite roadmap reaches the reader as an empty image container
ranked_recommendations.need: The chapter's only multi-step sequence, in its densest section, must reach the student in a form that shows the four operations in order.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: The spec is fully authored (five nodes, four steps, reagents, caveats) but no reader block type renders a synthesis_roadmap, so the compiler emits url "" and ReaderProviderImage falls back to alt text. Severity reconciled to high rather than the visual persona's blocker: the alt text does state all four operations in order and the prose names every reagent, so no learner is blocked — but the authored figure reaches nobody.

ranked_recommendations.title: Captions instruct the reader to find positions the render does not label
ranked_recommendations.need: Where a caption names a position, the reader must be able to find that position — or the caption must stop implying the figure shows it.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Enabling RDKit atom indices would actively mislead: they are 0-based traversal order, not chemical locants, so 'N9' would display as '8'. Each asset's alt_text and long_description already map every named position correctly, and long_description now reaches the reader. Rewriting the six offending captions to state the fact and defer to the description is therefore the least-complex fix that fully closes the caption/figure contract gap.

ranked_recommendations.title: Two stems promise a structure-reading task and show no structure
ranked_recommendations.need: An item whose stem tells the student to read a structure must present one, or must stop claiming it does.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Both items' options are prose statements about donor/acceptor patterns rather than structures to compare, so attaching structures would not change what the student actually evaluates. Rewording the two stems fully removes the false promise; adding a paired-base figure (rec-004) is the real remedy for the underlying skill.

ranked_recommendations.title: Markdown headings and list markers do not survive into the reader
ranked_recommendations.need: The subsection and step structure the author wrote must render as structure, not as literal '###' characters.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: RichText implements only bold and code by design. ch28 is the only package in the repo that used markdown headings, so this is a self-inflicted authoring defect rather than a platform gap; converting the three headings and four list markers to bold lead-ins is exact and immediate.

ranked_recommendations.title: Wikipedia titles use spaces, producing malformed links
ranked_recommendations.need: Every generated external link must resolve.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Seven concepts carry a wikipedia_title containing a space; the compiler interpolates it straight into a /wiki/ URL. House convention across the repo is underscores by 100 to 10, and all seven target pages return 200 when correctly encoded. Found by the orchestrator integrity check, not by a persona.

ranked_recommendations.title: Terms the assessment turns on are missing, under-defined, or untaught
ranked_recommendations.need: A student must not meet a graded term the chapter never defines, nor a reagent the chapter never names.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Bounded vocabulary repairs: define melting temperature at first substantive use; name pyrophosphorolysis in the standard tier; name dichloroacetic acid where detritylation is taught; drop N-methylimidazole from a rank_order card since it appears nowhere in the chapter; state the thymidine naming exception in the prose rather than only in a wrong-answer explanation; widen the ch28-capping-purpose accepted answers or tighten its prompt.

ranked_recommendations.title: teacher_optional metadata contradicts the prerequisite graph
ranked_recommendations.need: The optionality claim and the prerequisite graph must agree, or an instructor who drops concept 9 gets a concept 10 whose declared prerequisite is absent.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Two metadata defects of the same kind. concept 9's why_optional promises that nothing downstream depends on it while concept 10 lists it as a prerequisite and its prose refers back to 'the 2',3'-dideoxy analogues from the previous section'. Correcting the why_optional wording to declare the two optional concepts a single removable unit is exact and avoids touching the prerequisite graph the mastery gating uses. Separately, base-pairing-and-hydrogen-bonding does not declare phosphodiester-backbone as a prerequisite despite building its geometric argument on it, and chain-extension-at-phosphorus does not declare rna-versus-dna-hydrolytic-stability despite leaning on it explicitly; the linear reading order hides this, but concept maps and adaptive review read the declared graph.

ranked_recommendations.title: Three small chemical and notational defects
ranked_recommendations.need: A wrong-answer explanation must not misstate a product; a quantitative claim should match the literature; one SN2 rendering should be used throughout.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: All three are bounded factual corrections: beta-phosphorus attack delivers a diphosphate to the chain end, not 'a phosphate group'; the depurination-over-depyrimidination ratio is about 20-fold for DNA rather than two orders of magnitude, and the questions only rely on the qualitative claim; and 'S_N2' with a literal underscore reaches the compiled reader where 'SN2' is used everywhere else.

ranked_recommendations.title: The ribo ATP figure sits in a DNA-framed section without comment
ranked_recommendations.need: A figure that deliberately shows the ribo case immediately after two sections that made the deoxy case the point must say so, or it undercuts the distinction it sits beside.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: One sentence naming ATP as the generic triphosphate and noting that a DNA polymerase is handed the 2'-deoxy version turns an apparent inconsistency into a reinforcement. Swapping the figure to dATP would also work but would lose ATP's familiarity, which is why it was chosen.

ranked_recommendations.title: Beta configuration is defined by a drawing convention the chapter never shows
ranked_recommendations.need: The alpha/beta test ('same face as C5'') must be checkable on a figure that uses the representation the definition assumes.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: A Haworth-style pair showing both anomers is the only way to make the stated test performable; the current RDKit renders do not control ring orientation, so the test cannot be applied to them. Deferred as a recommendation rather than corrected, since it requires a new figure type for this package.

ranked_recommendations.title: Authored practice checks and section metadata never reach the reader
ranked_recommendations.need: Ten authored practice checks, three learning objectives per section, and the core/standard/advanced depth labels exist in the package and are dropped by the compiler.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Platform-level: the compiled section object supports only id/title/blocks. Recorded rather than corrected because it affects every chapter and needs a schema change, not a chapter edit.

ranked_recommendations.title: Four concepts have no entry-level question
ranked_recommendations.need: Each concept needs one low-stakes check a student can pass right after reading, especially the two whose only practice is advanced multi-field reasoning.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: nucleoside-analogue-drugs has exactly one item and it is advanced structured_reasoning; reading-and-writing-dna has two, both advanced. Recorded as a described recommendation rather than auto-corrected, since expanding the bank is a scope decision rather than an error repair.

ranked_recommendations.title: Question-stimulus alt text names the image instead of describing it
ranked_recommendations.need: Structures shown inside a question need alt text conveying what the sighted learner reads off the drawing, without disclosing the answer.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Platform-level: ErrorRepairRenderer hard-codes alt='Structure for the flawed step', and MatchingRenderer/ComparisonMatrixRenderer repeat the visible label. For the matching item this silently changes the task, since the compound name fully determines the answer.

ranked_recommendations.title: accessible_description is authored everywhere and rendered almost nowhere
ranked_recommendations.need: The stimulus description a learner needs must reach the surfaces where these question types are answered.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Platform-level and the multiplier on rec-002: only ReactionCoordinateQuestionRenderer and MolecularGeometryRenderer consume the field, and this chapter uses neither type. All 46 descriptions are well-written and inert at delivery.

ranked_recommendations.title: The compiled reader emits an inline link to the generic chapter landing page
ranked_recommendations.need: A chapter-level 'why this chapter' link tells a reader nothing and is explicitly disallowed by the production standard.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Compiler-generated for every chapter from the chapter number, not authored here; this chapter's own curated Additional Reading correctly carries four specific verified §28.x section links on a different surface. Recorded as a platform observation so it is not mistaken for an authoring defect.

ranked_recommendations.title: textbook_matching claims a one-to-one map that the chapter does not deliver
ranked_recommendations.need: An instructor assigning this chapter alongside OpenStax 28 must be told which textbook sections are out of scope rather than promised full coverage.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: The package's own note says OpenStax 28.1 to 28.8 map one to one, and lists 'polymerase chain reaction' among the matching terms, but no concept, nugget, asset or question covers PCR (28.8) or translation (28.5). Correcting the note is exact and honest; adding PCR content is a scope decision, and the Additional Reading panel already links both absent sections precisely so a reader can reach them.

visual_opportunities: A hydrogen-bonded base pair shown as a pair, for A-T, G-C and one rejected combination (rec-004).
A stepwise drawing of each of the two substitutions at phosphorus, showing nucleophile, electrophile and leaving group in one frame (rec-005).
